title: Buying Heuristics and Technical Signal Matrix: Redwood vs Managed Cloud Endpoints
body:
Purpose:
This note distills buying heuristics and observable technical signals that indicate a prospect is more likely to choose Redwood Inference over hyperscaler managed endpoints (AWS/GCP/Azure). The goal is to equip AE/SE with rapid diagnostics, tailored value anchors, and concrete rebuttals for common traps (cost framing, SLA promises, and security pushback).

Executive summary:
- Short thesis: Customers choose hyperscaler-managed endpoints when they prioritize easy model access and minimal operational ownership. They choose Redwood when they need predictable per-token economics at scale, deterministic latency, private deployment options, and operational controls (routing, rollouts, cache policies) that integrate with product SLAs.
- Quick win themes: (1) Predictable unit economics at scale; (2) Deployment parity across hosted / dedicated / private; (3) Operational controls that reduce on-call and incident surface; (4) Graceful degradation / fallback strategies.

Buyer personas and their primary signals:
- Platform/Infra Lead (Platform teams): Signals: requests for routing policies, desire to standardize inference across BU, references to "vendor lock-in" concerns, questions about network egress and VPC integrations. Value anchor: unified API + private control plane + versioned rollouts for safety-critical apps.
- ML Engineer / MLE: Signals: model-level metrics, latency-percentile obsession (p95/p99), experimentation velocity concerns, questions on KV cache and batching. Value anchor: kernel-aware serving runtime, continuous batching, quantization guidance, and prebuilt eval hooks.
- Product Owner (chat/agent features): Signals: deterministic UX latency targets (<200ms), streaming & function calling support, fallbacks when model fails. Value anchor: fast streaming + automatic fallback to cheaper model variants, precise cost per conversation metrics.
- Security/Compliance / Legal: Signals: data residency, audit logs, KMS/HSM integration, SOC reports. Value anchor: private deployment and audit-ready telemetry.

Decision criteria matrix (what buyers care about) - observable signals and Redwood messaging:
1) Latency predictability:
- Signal: customer cites p99/p95 targets or complains about tail latency in experiments.
- Redwood message: predictable kernels + routing policies + autoscaling tuned for SLOs; show latency breakdown per token in Console.

2) Unit cost transparency and optimization:
- Signal: questions about per-token unit economics, desire for caching/batching recommendations.
- Redwood message: Optimize tool gives batching/quantization suggestions and expected cost delta; show sample ROI for 1M monthly tokens.

3) Operational ownership / control:
- Signal: mentions multi-tenant risk, need for canary rollouts, or multi-region failover.
- Redwood message: rollout primitives (canary, A/B, auto-fallback), smart routing by region/price/latency.

4) Private deployments & compliance:
- Signal: "air-gapped", on-prem, VPC-only, or strict KMS needs.
- Redwood message: Private control plane and on-prem packages; demonstrate audit log samples and KMS integration playbook.

5) SLA & reliability assurances:
- Signal: RFP asks for uptime/latency SLAs, incident MTTR targets.
- Redwood message: Dedicated reserved capacity + SLA commitments + graceful fallback tiers and circuit-breaker policies.

6) Model ecosystem & freshness:
- Signal: preference for hyperscaler model catalog or proprietary model hosting.
- Redwood message: support for open models, pinned versions, easy onboarding for custom models, and automatic kernel selection for performance.

Competitive posture vs AWS/GCP/Azure (short bullets, not exhaustive):
- Where hyperscalers are stronger: seamless billing consolidation, single-console integration for cloud-native apps, broad model catalogs (managed large models from cloud partners).
- Where Redwood is stronger: inference economics at scale, observability tied to token-level cost, deployment parity across private/hosted/dedicated, richer rollout & fallback policies, and SRE-friendly operational tooling.

Common AE/SE framing scripts (quick):
- For Platform: "If you want to prevent per-tenant surprises and maintain the same inference API across dev/prod/on-prem, Redwood lets you own the SLOs while reducing the maintenance burden via our rollout and tracing primitives."
- For MLE: "We surface kernel and sequence-length tradeoffs so you don't have to rewrite ops code; our Optimize recommendations often cut inference cost 20–40% on production workloads."
- For Security: "We can deploy a customer-managed control plane with HSM/KMS integration and provide audit artifacts ready for SOC reviews."

Top objections and rebuttals:
- Objection: "Hyperscaler is cheaper at our current scale — we get discounts and managed model access."
  Rebuttal: "Let's model your real-monthly token mix and show three levers (batching, KV caching, quantization) and the expected delta — many customers see break-even within weeks as usage grows and tail latency constraints tighten."

- Objection: "We want the convenience of one cloud console for everything."
  Rebuttal: "Redwood integrates with cloud infra for billing and IAM; our differentiator is providing operational controls and predictable per-token economics across environments — we can show integration architecture in 30 mins."

- Objection: "Security wants a hyperscaler due to existing contracts."
  Rebuttal: "We routinely work with procurement and security: offer an on-prem test slice, share SOC artifacts, and propose a pilot under their contractual guardrails — we can scope a short on-prem POC with limited data."

Demo/POC framework (30/60/90 day):
- Day 0–7: discovery + lightweight perf eval (existing sample prompts or prod traces).
- Week 2–4: deploy Redwood hosted with dedicated pool; run A/B: same prompts to hyperscaler managed endpoint and Redwood, capture cost/latency and quality metrics.
- Month 1+: escalate to private/dedicated deployment for traffic mimic; enable Optimize suggestions; present ROI and run canary rollouts to show operational primitives.

Tactical playbook for SEs (checklist):
- Pre-call: ask for p95/p99 SLAs, monthly token budget, and model(s) in use.
- Bring: a sample cost model template and a short demo notebook comparing latencies and cost.
- During POC: enable tracing, record token-level cost, and run the Optimize recommendations; highlight fallback behavior on simulated overload.

Collateral and quick artifacts to share:
- One-pager: "How Redwood cuts inference cost without trading latency" (include sample ROI).
- Technical appendix: "Private deployment checklist" with network diagram and KMS steps.
- Eval kit: small dataset + script to run concurrent queries and capture p95/p99 and per-token cost.

Open questions / things to validate with product teams:
- Add a simple SLO-preserving cost estimator we can run live in demo (inputs: tokens/month, percent streaming, p99 target).
- Create a short audit artifact package for security reviews (templates for SOC, KMS config, logging fields).

Appendix: sample discovery questions (use in first 10 mins)
- What p95/p99 latency targets do you need for user-facing features?
- How predictable do you need per-conversation costs to be? Are you on a fixed budget?
- Do you have requirements for on-prem vs cloud or specific region constraints?
- Who owns incident response for inference outages today?

This document should be used by AEs and SEs as a rapid diagnostic + framing checklist. Aim to keep the sales conversation anchored to measurable signals (latency percentiles, token spend, security constraints) and to move quickly to a short A/B perf/ROI POC rather than philosophical debates about cloud vendor lock-in.

Notes: draft — will iterate with product and SEs to capture up-to-date Optimize ROI numbers and POC templates.
